samples.summary: The evidence <details> fold is never asserted to render — the only evidence test asserts it is DROPPED
samples.evidence: blockingEvidence() (review-comment.mjs:96-100) builds the `<details><summary>evidence</summary>` block and the rebuild loop at :254-267 exists solely to place folds under their findings. The only test touching evidence is "oversized blocking evidence never drops a blocking finding" (review-comment.test.mjs), which passes maxChars:1200 with 5000-char evidence and asserts `!out.includes(big)` — i.e. it asserts the fold is ABSENT. No test ever renders a blocking finding with small evidence under a normal budget and asserts the `<details><summary>evidence</summary>` markup, the two-space indentation of multi-line evidence (`.replace(/\n/g, "\n  ")`), or that the fold sits under its own finding. The whole rebuild branch (the `if (shown.some(...))` path producing output) could emit garbage markup and every test would still pass.

samples.summary: mergedNote() (the "also reported as" fold) has no test at all, despite the module claiming merged wordings are "never silently dropped"
samples.evidence: mergedNote() at review-comment.mjs:72-80 renders `<details><summary>also reported as (N)</summary>` with each merged wording's normalized severity, and is the stated guarantee that clustering never silently deletes a wording. `grep -n 'mergedFrom' scripts/agent/review-comment.test.mjs` returns no hits: no fixture in the test file sets `mergedFrom`, so this function is executed only via the `.length` short-circuit returning "". A regression that dropped merged wordings entirely (e.g. returning "" unconditionally) would keep the suite green.

samples.summary: The `unsettled` ("verifier could not settle this") marker on blocking and minor rows is untested
samples.evidence: blockingHead (review-comment.mjs:89) and minorRow (:109) both append " _(verifier could not settle this)_" when `f.unsettled`. No test fixture sets `unsettled` — grep for 'unsettled' in review-comment.test.mjs has zero hits. The marker exists precisely so a reader does not read an unfiltered claim as confirmed (severity.mjs:70 rationale); silently losing it in this renderer would not fail any test.

samples.summary: The green "🟢 Review panel: looks good" header branch is never asserted
samples.evidence: The `blocked` computation (:168-171) selects between 🔴 and 🟢. Only the 🔴 branch is asserted ("headline counts + verdict…": `assert.match(out, /^### 🔴 Review panel: changes suggested/)` and the CLI test). Tests that produce a success conclusion (the minor/nit collapse test) assert nothing about the header, so an inverted or always-🔴 verdict line would pass. The gating/applicable exclusions in the same predicate (`gating !== false`, `applicable !== false`) are likewise never exercised — every `lens()` helper hardcodes `gating: true, applicable: true`.

samples.summary: collectLenses' gating/applicable/unverified mapping is untested; only id/findings/conclusion are asserted
samples.evidence: collectLenses maps `gating: String(lens.gating ?? "blocking") === "blocking"`, `applicable: p.applicable !== false`, and passes through `unverified`. The test "collectLenses merges verdict.json + panel.json in manifest order" asserts only `length`, `got[0].id`, `findings.length`, `conclusion`, plus the missing-dir fallback. The fixture manifest uses `gating: "blocking"` for both lenses and no `applicable: false` / `unverified` entries, so a non-blocking lens (gating other than "blocking") or an inapplicable lens is never exercised end-to-end — the field could be inverted and the suite stays green.
searchedFor: read fakeReviewDir() and the collectLenses test in review-comment.test.mjs

samples.summary: Blocking sort order (critical before major, then manifest lens order) is asserted only indirectly
samples.evidence: blockingSorted (:193-196) sorts by rankSev, then lens manifest order, then discovery order. The one test with both a critical and a major ("headline counts + verdict, blocking expanded and first") asserts `blkIdx < detIdx` and matches the critical row's markup, but never asserts that "boom" appears before "leak" in the output. Removing the sort entirely would not fail any test.
searchedFor: read the 'headline counts + verdict' test assertions

samples.summary: The relocated `contentSha` proof branch is exercised but never asserted
samples.evidence: relocatedRow (:117-121) has two proof branches. The relocated test asserts only the `alsoAt` branch (`/this line already exists at `old\.ts:9`/`). The preservation test does include a finding with `novelty: { contentSha: "abcdef123" }` (test line ~127) but asserts only that the finding's summary text survives, never the "content dates to `abcdef123`, which predates the base" line or the 9-char sha truncation. That branch can break silently.

samples.summary: The CLI's empty-output path — the exact condition the workflow's fallback depends on — is never tested
samples.evidence: The workflow reads /tmp/review-comment.md and falls back to the old per-lens concatenation when it is empty (`if (!region) region = ...`). renderReviewComment returning "" is unit-tested, but the CLI test only covers the populated case: it never runs the CLI over a review dir with no findings to assert that --out is written as an empty file (rather than left missing/containing stale content) and that nothing is echoed to stdout. That is the contract the workflow's fail-safe rests on.
searchedFor: read the 'CLI writes the rendered region to --out and echoes it' test

verdict.reason: Verified independently. mergedNote() exists at scripts/agent/review-comment.mjs:72-80 and renders the "also reported as (N)" fold from f.mergedFrom, reached via blockingEvidence() (line 99) from renderReviewComment (lines 254, 259). I read all 223 lines of scripts/agent/review-comment.test.mjs: the fixture builder F() (line 12) is never called with mergedFrom, and no test asserts on "also reported as", so mergedNote is only ever exercised through its `if (!m.length) return ""` short-circuit — a regression returning "" unconditionally would keep the suite green. I searched wider for an indirect counterexample: repo-wide grep for mergedFrom/mergedNote/"also reported as" hits only severity.test.mjs, review-panel.test.mjs, rebuttal.test.mjs and .trusted copies. The one test that actually renders the fold, severity.test.mjs:112-123, targets renderSummaryMd in severity.mjs — a separate duplicated implementation; review-comment.mjs imports only BLOCKING and normalizeSeverity from severity.mjs (line 25), so that test cannot fail on a review-comment.mjs regression. Grep for any importer/reference of review-comment across the repo returns only the test, the module, docs, the on-demand workflow, and generated .agent-review artifacts; there is no .trusted/scripts/agent/review-comment* variant. Even the CLI end-to-end fixture (test lines 181-199) writes verdict.json findings without mergedFrom. The module's own stated guarantee (lines 69-71, "never silently dropped") is therefore shipped with no meaningful test — a clear behavior branch with zero coverage, which is major under the test-adequacy rubric.
